title: Optimal Ansatz-free Hamiltonian Learning In Situ
claim: Our protocol needs only simple, control-free evolution on the system, whereas general learning interleaves ancillas and control operations.
layout: 2 panels, left-to-right, circuit-style diagrams with simple (a) versus interleaved (b)
description: Two circuit-style diagrams side by side, labeled (a) and (b), drawn in dark navy line art on white. Panel (a), at left, shows three horizontal qubit wires running through one large rounded box labeled e^{-iHt}, with left and right pointed arrow-shaped brackets framing it as state preparation and measurement. Panel (b), at right, is wider and has the same framing brackets. It shows two black qubit wires plus a light grey wire on top for the ancilla qubit. Along the wires, evolution boxes e^{-iHt_1}, e^{-iHt_2}, ..., e^{-iHt_m} alternate with control unitary boxes U_1, ..., U_{m-1}, separated by an ellipsis. The contrast between the single block and the long interleaved sequence is what the eye reads first.
caption: (a) Control-free ancilla-free Hamiltonian learning protocols considered in this work. (b) The general Hamiltonian learning settings with ancillary qubits (grey qubits) and quantum control.
abstract: Characterizing the features of a Hamiltonian that governs a quantum system serves as a fundamental subroutine of quantum device calibration, signal sensing, and error correction. Recent works have proposed protocols achieving the optimal Heisenberg-limited scaling learning ansatz-free Hamiltonians from their real-time evolutions without fully specifying interaction structures. However, these protocols rely on both deep circuits with interleaving probes and control, and extremely short time resolution, making them difficult to implement on near- and intermediate-term in situ quantum experiments. In this work, we propose a computationally efficient, control-free, and ancilla-free algorithm that uses only Pauli product state preparation and measurement, and learns an ansatz-free Hamiltonian $H$ with $||H||\leqÎ$ in total evolution time of $Î(\fracÎ{Îµ^2}\log(\fracÎÎµ))$. The evolution time cost of our algorithm is optimal for any control-free protocols as we further prove a lower bound of $Î©(\fracÎ{Îµ^2}\log(\fracÎÎµ))$. Technically, our method introduces a randomized-sampling framework that combines band-limited kernel-based time sampling with a displacement sieve for Hamiltonian structure learning. The characteristic probe time resolution depends only on $Î$ instead of $\varepsilon$, which makes our protocol especially appealing in the high-precision regime for sensing and calibration applications. We also show that the algorithm maintains the same asymptotic total evolution time in the presence of state-preparation-and-measurement (SPAM) noise when the Hamiltonian is local after calibration. Our results demonstrate the fundamental cost of experimentally friendly Hamiltonian learning and provide a practical route to rigorous in situ characterization of near-term quantum platforms.
